title: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI Use Lean 4 to Discover Formally Verified Quantum Algorithms - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used multi-agent Gemini teams inside the Lean 4 theorem prover with quantum Hoare logic to discover formally verified fault-tolerant quantum programs, cutting logical spacetime cost (Q·T) by 2.5x to >290x on benchmarks from arithmetic to fusion and drug metabolism.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI built an automated quantum algorithm discovery pipeline where LLM agents work inside the Lean 4 theorem prover using quantum Hoare logic, enabling synthesis and machine-checked verification of quantum programs beyond classical simulation scale.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-driven, provably correct algorithm design could compress the timeline to useful fault-tolerant applications — a Google edge.
insights.locator: Researchers from Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI

insights.claim: Classical simulation cannot validate quantum algorithms at thousands of logical qubits, so the Google team specified problems in Lean 4 as formal Hoare triples with proofs of correctness and resource bounds instead of testing by simulation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Formal verification solves the 'how do you trust AI-designed circuits at scale' problem.

insights.claim: In the discovery loop, heterogeneous Gemini agent teams exchange lemmas, verified code and critiques via a shared wiki and scheduled conferences, while an independent Lean comparator checks proofs against frozen specifications with no custom axioms or unproven placeholders.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A reusable template for AI-for-science research: multi-agent search gated by an incorruptible verifier.

insights.claim: Fault-tolerant cost is measured as Q·T (peak logical qubits times non-Clifford T-gate count) because surface-code lattice surgery makes Clifford gates cheap, so magic-state preparation dominates physical spacetime footprint.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Q·T reductions translate directly into smaller/cheaper fault-tolerant machines needed for useful workloads.
insights.quote: preparing non-Clifford magic states dominates hardware execution cycles, making Q · T a primary proxy for physical spacetime footprint

insights.claim: Agent-discovered 25-bit fixed-point arcsin state preparation cut Q·T by more than 290x (from over 1.08 × 10^8 to 3.70 × 10^5), using 3,698 T gates across 100 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Large arithmetic-subroutine savings propagate across many fault-tolerant algorithms.

insights.claim: For alpha-particle stopping power in warm dense hydrogen (inertial-confinement fusion), the verified program lowered Q·T 10.9x to 4.98 × 10^14 on 4,374 logical qubits by moving to a real-space grid and using Pauli exclusion to truncate redundant short-range Coulomb terms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude cost cuts bring fusion-relevant simulations closer to feasible fault-tolerant hardware.

insights.claim: For non-Born–Oppenheimer dynamics of C23H20N3O, agents cut Q·T 8.08x on 6,057 logical qubits by replacing swap networks with measurement-based ancilla uncomputation and using Bernstein polynomial sampling for 1/r potentials.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows AI agents finding non-obvious circuit techniques, not just parameter tuning.

insights.claim: For cytochrome P450 Compound I, replacing binary table lookups with one-hot orbital registers cut T-gates per walk step by 40% and improved overall Q·T 2.49x on 333 logical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Drug-metabolism chemistry — a flagship pharma use case — gets cheaper to run on future fault-tolerant machines.

insights.claim: For multi-target parallel Grover search (m, k ≤ 1,024), collective Johnson-graph quantum walks gave up to 1.22x fewer expected oracle rounds to find any target and up to 2.55x to find all targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Even textbook algorithms still have AI-discoverable improvements.
